For this project, I collected my data by scraping publicly available college football statistics from ESPN. I already had a copy of the dataset saved from earlier work, so I used the ESPN site to double‑check the numbers and make sure everything matched the official statistics before running my analysis.

For this project, I’m studying how 4th‑down efficiency and performance relate to overall team strength, and whether there’s a significant difference between the best and worst teams of that season.

(Rank) is a variable I added myself based on ESPN’s Football Power Index (FPI) for that year. FPI is a mathematical rating system that accounts for a team’s overall performance and efficiency. It’s more reliable than the AP Poll because it removes human opinion and focuses entirely on data.

(4th‑down efficiency) is measured using the number of 4th‑down attempts, conversions, and the conversion rate.

(4th‑down ranking) shows how each team ranks nationally on 4th‑down performance compared to other teams in the same season.

Before running my analysis I had to do several things to clean the data to make sure it was prepared for me. First thing I did was filter out the select teams that I wanted for the two seperate seaons - 2014 and 2020. My next step was to fix the column names in the 2020 data set and cros-referenced the ESPN official site to make sure I was labeling them correctly and the stats for the designated column was correct.I also built my own rank column for the teams using ESPNS' Football Power Index(FPI) since it was not originally included in the data set. Once I was able to cross reference everything and establish the validity of the data, I filtered out the specific rows that I wanted such as 'Wins' 'Rank' '4th down efficiency', etc so I wasnt dealing with 150 unnecessary columns.

plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))
sns.barplot(
    data=data14_compare,
    x="Team",
    y="X4th.Percent",
    hue="Group",
    palette={"Top 25": "#08FF10", "Bottom 25": "#750902"}
)
plt.title("2014 Top 25 vs Bottom 25: 4th Down Efficiency", fontsize=16, weight="bold")
plt.ylabel("4th Down Conversion Rate")
plt.xlabel("Team")
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

I wanted to print out the individual teams here to see who really was excelling amongst the teams We notice here that some of the worst teams in the nation FPI wise were not that bad on 4th down efficiency with many converting at a rate near or over 50%. What I found interesting here is that Florida State actually did not attempt a single 4th down this entire year.

    palette={"Top 25": "#152FF8", "Bottom 25": "#F541B9"}

plt.ylabel("4th Down Attempts")
plt.xlabel("Team")
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

I wondered if some of the bad teams were attempting more 4th downs due to having a potentially struggling offense and not being able to pick up 10 in 3 downs, however Baylor this year by far had the most attempts this particular year while also having the number 1 overall offense. In fact you notice a lot of the bottom tier teams seem to have played it really conservative this year such as Eastern Michigan and Southern Mississippi

bottom_avg = bottom25["x4th.percentage"].mean()

plt.bar(["Top 25", "Bottom 25"], [top_avg, bottom_avg], color=["Green", "Red"])

plt.title("Average 4th Down Efficiency: Top 25 vs Bottom 25 Teams")
plt.show()

X = comparison["Rank"]
y = comparison["x4th.percentage"]

X2 = sm.add_constant(X)
model = sm.OLS(y, X2).fit()

comparison["predicted"] = model.predict(X2)

Conclusion¶

This analysis explores whether top‑ranked college football teams perform better on 4th‑down plays than bottom‑ranked teams. The results show that while top teams generally have higher conversion percentages, the differences are not always consistent across seasons and sometimes very minuscule. Contextual factors such as opponent strength, game situation, and coaching strategy likely influence these outcomes. Overall, the data suggests that team ranking alone does not fully explain 4th‑down success and vice versa 4th-down success does not explain team rank, highlighting the complexity of decision‑making in football analytics.

Ethics and Limitations¶

My research question asks whether top‑ranked teams are better than bottom‑ranked teams on 4th‑down plays. There are multiple limitations to this analysis because many different factors can influence 4th‑down outcomes — from weather conditions and field distance to how efficient an offense is on 3rd down, which determines whether a 4th‑down situation is manageable.

Dataset limitations: One of the seasons in this dataset (2020) occurred during the COVID‑19 pandemic, meaning shortened schedules and fewer games. The dataset also lacks contextual variables such as opponent strength, play‑calling decisions, and penalties (pre‑snap or post‑snap) that could nullify plays.

Research question limitations: While the analysis compares conversion rates between top and bottom teams, it cannot explain why those differences occur. Factors like coaching strategy, risk tolerance, and game context are not captured in the data. These limitations mean the results should be interpreted as general patterns rather than definitive conclusions.

Code and AI transparency: Copilot AI only used to help with syntax for combining columns from seperate years and data sets to compare.
